item.title: Compromised TLS Certificates
item.author: Bruce Schneier
item.content:encoded: The compromised eMudhra keys were defective at a level that’s challenging the imagination of many of the engineers studying the incident. A normal size for a NIST P-384 elliptic curve cryptography private key contains roughly 384 bits of entropy, a size allowing almost 2, or a number with 116 digits, different possibilities. The private key sizes of the compromised keys ranged from 3 to 8 bits. Astonishingly, the private keys were 4, 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230, 237.“That is extremely in the ‘this should not be possible’ category,” Valdorda said. “Maybe some horribly dangerous key generation interface has a ‘size’ parameter and they set it to 1 by mistake???”Ben Cartwright-Cox, director of BGP.tools, said: “My guess is that it’s example code that accidentally leaked to production, but hard to know. But it’s bonkers that no one noticed.”At this early stage, the most immediate threat appears to be for those using VPNs, especially in countries with governments likely to maliciously intercept traffic. There are likely many other cases for concern. End users largely have no recourse other than to hold off using many non-browser forms of TLS communication until they receive assurances updates are in place.The whole certificate regime has long been a mess:The incident is the latest to expose a fatal flaw in the TLS regimen. It’s only as strong as its weakest link, which in this case was eMudhra. Fortunately, transparency logs account for much of that failure, but this measure requires parties to actively monitor massive feeds and works only after unauthorized certificates have been issued. eMudhra representatives weren’t immediately available to answer questions.One caveat: exploiting compromised certificates requires an active adversary-in-the-middle attack, meaning the attacker must act as a proxy between two TLS parties and receive encrypted traffic, decrypt it, reencrypt it, and send it to the other party. Such capabilities, in some cases, are usually limited to only the most well-resourced attackers. People with control of a local network­at a coffee shop, university, or other organization­face much less of a challenge.Cleanup of this is going to be another mess—and it’s right on top of the PHP vulnerabilities.

item.title: New Serious PHP Vulnerabilities Released and Patched
item.author: Bruce Schneier
item.content:encoded: PHP maintainers have released fixes for two critical vulnerabilities:PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 fix two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately. Who is at risk: all PHP installations serving web requests, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs.RCE via OOM corruption, CVE-2026-109618 (GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w): out-of-memory handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid. RCE via stale global state, CVE-2026-109619 (GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp): request-owned internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it.Updating PHP is the only way to regain security. Do it now.

item.title: Siemens SIMATIC S7 Webserver API
item.author: CISA
item.content:encoded: .NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API contains multiple vulnerabilities that could allow an attacker to obtain sensitive information or write arbitrary files outside the intended download directory. Siemens has released a new version for .NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API and recommends to update to the latest version.The following versions of Siemens SIMATIC S7 Webserver API are affected:.NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API vers:intdot/<3.3.61, vers:intdot/<3.3.62 (CVE-2026-85114, CVE-2026-85115).NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver APIImproper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal'), Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive InformationCritical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and FacilitiesCountries/Areas Deployed: WorldwideCompany Headquarters Location: GermanyAffected applications do not properly validate filenames received from remote servers during ticket downloads. This could allow an attacker who can manipulate the ticket response to write arbitrary files outside the intended download directory and, when overwriting is enabled, replace existing files accessible to the application..NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API < V3.3.61Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V3.3.61 or later versionAffected applications do not properly redact PLC restore passwords from HTTP error exception messages. This could allow an attacker with access to logs or other diagnostic output to obtain the plaintext restore password and potentially perform unauthorized operations on the PLC..NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API < V3.3.61Product Status: known_affected.NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API < V3.3.62Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V3.3.62 or later versionSiemens ProductCERT reported these vulnerabilities to CISA.As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurityFor further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisoriesThe use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.Advisory Conversion DisclaimerThis ICSA is a verbatim republication of Siemens ProductCERT SSA-390352 from a direct conversion of the vendor's Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF) advisory. item.title: Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808 Devices
item.author: CISA
item.content:encoded: Nozomi Networks has published information on vulnerabilities in Nozomi Guardian/CMC. This advisory lists the related Siemens Industrial products affected by these vulnerabilities. Siemens recommends to contact customer support to receive patch and update information.The following versions of Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808 Devices are affected:RUGGEDCOM APE1808 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-33387, CVE-2026-33388, CVE-2026-33389, CVE-2026-33391, CVE-2026-33920)Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine, Incorrect Authorization, Lack of Administrator Control over Security, Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and FacilitiesCountries/Areas Deployed: WorldwideCompany Headquarters Location: GermanyA template injection vulnerability was discovered in the Dashboards functionality due to improper validation of an input parameter. An authenticated user with the required privileges can define a dashboard containing a malicious payload, or a victim can be socially engineered into importing a malicious dashboard. When the victim views or imports the dashboard, the payload executes in their browser context, allowing the attacker to modify application data or disrupt application availability.RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationAn access control vulnerability was discovered in the Credentials Manager functionality due to insufficient validation of user privileges. A remote authenticated user with limited privileges can view a limited subset of the available entries in the Credentials Manager. The actual credential values are not directly visible, but the user can delete entries or edit their properties. An attacker who deletes or edits an entry can disrupt authentication for dependent devices, and one who manipulates an entry's configuration may be able to indirectly obtain the credentials.RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationRUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationAn improper certificate/host key validation vulnerability was discovered in the Smart Polling functionality, which established encrypted connections to target devices without validating the remote host's identity, and no option was provided to enable it. A man-in-the-middle attacker positioned between a sensor and a polled device can, during a polling session, impersonate the device and intercept the communication, including the credentials used to access it. The captured credentials can then be replayed to authenticate against the device itself or against other devices sharing the same credentials, allowing the attacker to access and tamper with the device's data and to disrupt its operations.RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationRUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationRUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationAn access control vulnerability was discovered in the Smart Polling configuration functionality due to insufficient validation of user privileges. An authenticated user with limited privileges can remotely bypass the intended access control of the web management interface and modify the Smart Polling discovery configuration. This allows the attacker to disrupt the visibility of assets in the monitored network.RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationRUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationRUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationRUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationA cross-site request forgery vulnerability was discovered in the login functionality (both standard and SAML) due to missing validation of the anti-CSRF token. An attacker with a valid account can trick a victim into unknowingly authenticating with the attacker's credentials. Any operation performed by the victim in this state is attributed to the attacker's account, compromising the integrity of the audit trail.RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationRUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationRUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationRUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationRUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationSiemens ProductCERT reported these vulnerabilities to CISA.As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurityFor further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisoriesThe use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. item.title: Siemens RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller
item.author: CISA
item.content:encoded: RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) contains multiple vulnerabilities in the integrated SQLite component that could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code, cause a denial of service, or obtain sensitive information. Siemens has released a new version for RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) and recommends to update to the latest version.The following versions of Siemens RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller are affected:RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) vers:intdot/<6.0 (CVE-2025-6965, CVE-2025-70873, CVE-2025-71316, CVE-2026-11822, CVE-2026-11824)RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC)Numeric Truncation Error, Improper Clearing of Heap Memory Before Release ('Heap Inspection'), Improper Handling of Unicode Encoding, Heap-based Buffer OverflowCritical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and FacilitiesCountries/Areas Deployed: WorldwideCompany Headquarters Location: GermanyThere exists a vulnerability in SQLite versions before 3.50.2 where the number of aggregate terms could exceed the number of columns available. This could lead to a memory corruption issue. We recommend upgrading to version 3.50.2 or above.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionAn information disclosure issue in the zipfileInflate function in the zipfile extension in SQLite v3.51.1 and earlier allows attackers to obtain heap memory via supplying a crafted ZIP file.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionSQLite 'sqldiff.exe' does not securely handle the way the Microsoft Windows C runtime converts Unicode characters to ANSI codepages. An attacker could use the '-L' option to load an arbitrary DLL with a crafted command line argument string that results in command line file arguments being misinterpreted as command line options. Fixed on or around 2025-12-26.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionSQLite before 3.53.2 contains memory corruption vulnerabilities in the FTS5 full-text search extension that allow attackers to cause process crashes, memory exhaustion, or arbitrary code execution by supplying a crafted database with malformed FTS5 page data. Attackers can trigger an out-of-bounds read in fts5LeafSeek() via an attacker-controlled loop bound and a heap buffer overflow write in fts5ChunkIterate() through a crafted continuation page causing an integer underflow, exploitable when an FTS5 MATCH query is executed against the malicious database.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionSQLite before 3.53.2 contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the FTS5 full-text search extension that allows attackers to cause a crash or execute arbitrary code by supplying a crafted database with malicious continuation page metadata specifying a szLeaf value smaller than 4. Attackers can trigger an integer underflow in fts5ChunkIterate() causing an inflated remaining byte count during FTS5 MATCH query processing, leading to a heap buffer overflow of attacker-controlled data in applications compiled with SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionSiemens ProductCERT reported these vulnerabilities to CISA.As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurityFor further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisoriesThe use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.Advisory Conversion DisclaimerThis ICSA is a verbatim republication of Siemens ProductCERT SSA-765416 from a direct conversion of the vendor's Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF) advisory. This is republished to CISA's website as a means of increasing visibility and is provided "as-is" for informational purposes only. CISA is not responsible for the editorial or technical accuracy of republished advisories and provides no warranties of any kind regarding any information contained within this advisory. Further, CISA does not endorse any commercial product or service. Please contact Siemens ProductCERT directly for any questions regarding this advisory.2026-10-13Initial CISA Republication of Siemens ProductCERT SSA-765416 advisoryLegal Notice and Terms of Use

item.title: Siemens WinCC
item.author: CISA
item.content:encoded: Multiple SIMATIC WinCC versions are affected by a database privilege escalation vulnerability that could allow an authenticated user with access to the database to execute commands on the underlying host system. Siemens has released new versions for several affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions. Siemens is preparing further fixes and recommends mitigations for products where fixes are not or not yet available.The following versions of Siemens WinCC are affected:SIMATIC WinCC V7.5 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-59241)SIMATIC WinCC V8.0 vers:intdot/<8.0.0.11 (CVE-2026-59241)SIMATIC WinCC V8.1 vers:intdot/<8.1.7 (CVE-2026-59241)Incorrect Privilege AssignmentCritical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and FacilitiesCountries/Areas Deployed: WorldwideCompany Headquarters Location: GermanyThe affected application does not sufficiently restrict the permissions assigned to a database role. This could allow an authenticated remote attacker with database access to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary commands on the host system where SIMATIC WinCC is installed, potentially leading to a compromise of the system.Product Status: known_affectedCurrently no fix is availableSIMATIC WinCC V8.0 < V8.0 Update 11Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V8.0 Update 11 or later versionSIMATIC WinCC V8.1 < V8.1 Update 7Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V8.1 Update 7 or later versionSiemens ProductCERT reported this vulnerability to CISA.As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurityFor further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisoriesThe use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.Advisory Conversion DisclaimerThis ICSA is a verbatim republication of Siemens ProductCERT SSA-550198 from a direct conversion of the vendor's Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF) advisory. This is republished to CISA's website as a means of increasing visibility and is provided "as-is" for informational purposes only. CISA is not responsible for the editorial or technical accuracy of republished advisories and provides no warranties of any kind regarding any information contained within this advisory. Further, CISA does not endorse any commercial product or service. Please contact Siemens ProductCERT directly for any questions regarding this advisory.2026-10-13Initial CISA Republication of Siemens ProductCERT SSA-550198 advisoryLegal Notice and Terms of Use

item.title: Siemens RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW
item.author: CISA
item.content:encoded: RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW contains multiple vulnerabilities that could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary SQL commands on the underlying database, retrieve sensitive administrative credentials, escalate privileges, and perform unauthorized operations such as modifying system configurations or causing a denial of service. Siemens has released a new version for RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW and recommends to update to the latest version.The following versions of Siemens RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW are affected:RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW vers:intdot/<6.0 (CVE-2026-89196, CVE-2026-89197, CVE-2026-89198, CVE-2026-89199, CVE-2026-89200, CVE-2026-89201, CVE-2026-89202, CVE-2026-89203, CVE-2026-89204, CVE-2026-89205, CVE-2026-89206)Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection'), Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key, Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data, Client-Side Enforcement of Server-Side SecurityCritical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and FacilitiesCountries/Areas Deployed: WorldwideCompany Headquarters Location: GermanyAffected devices do not properly validate or sanitize input in facility names processed during the Bulk Import/Export workflow. This could allow an authenticated attacker with specific privileges to execute arbitrary SQL commands on the underlying database.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionAffected devices do not properly validate or sanitize input in the Value field of notification conditions processed during the Notification Profile configuration. This could allow an authenticated attacker with specific privileges to execute arbitrary SQL commands on the underlying database.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionAffected devices do not properly validate or sanitize the filename of firmware files uploaded to the system. This could allow an authenticated attacker with specific privileges to execute arbitrary SQL commands on the underlying database.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionAffected devices do not properly restrict access to sensitive configuration items via specific database queries. This could allow an authenticated attacker to retrieve administrative credentials for various internal systems, leading to unauthorized information disclosure and privilege escalation.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionAffected devices do not properly validate or sanitize input in the Name and Value fields for custom file labels. This could allow an authenticated attacker with administrative privileges to execute arbitrary SQL commands on the underlying database.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionAffected devices do not properly validate or sanitize input in device group or facility names processed during the Bulk Export workflow. This could allow an authenticated attacker with specific privileges to execute arbitrary SQL commands on the underlying database.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionAffected devices do not properly perform authorization checks for device disconnection requests. This could allow an authenticated attacker with minimal privileges to disconnect active sessions of other users, including administrators, leading to a denial of service.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionAffected devices do not properly restrict access to various database queries, allowing users to retrieve system-wide information that is not intended for their privilege level. This could allow an authenticated attacker to gather sensitive information about the system's infrastructure, including details on all devices, substations, users, and scheduled activities.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionAffected devices do not properly restrict access to database queries used for subnet management. This could allow an authenticated attacker to read, modify, or delete subnet configurations, leading to unauthorized information disclosure and data manipulation.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionAffected devices do not properly perform server-side authorization checks for requests to schedule special operations. This could allow an authenticated attacker with minimal privileges to schedule unauthorized operations on devices.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionAffected devices do not properly perform server-side authorization checks for requests to modify the state of scheduled actions. This could allow an authenticated attacker with minimal privileges to retry, stop, or delete scheduled tasks without proper authorization.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionSiemens ProductCERT reported these vulnerabilities to CISA.As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. item.title: Siemens SIMATIC IPCs
item.author: CISA
item.content:encoded: The products listed below contain a vulnerability that could allow an attacker to boot an operating system or UEFI application signed with that test key, bypassing UEFI Secure Boot protections even when Secure Boot is enabled. Siemens has released new versions for the affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions.The following versions of Siemens SIMATIC IPCs are affected:SIMATIC IPC BX-21A vers:intdot/<31.01.13 (CVE-2026-72895)SIMATIC IPC RW-543A vers:intdot/<1.1.4 (CVE-2026-72895)SIMATIC IPC227G / IPC277G / IPC277G PRO / IPC327G / IPC377G vers:intdot/<28.01.15 (CVE-2026-72895)Use of Default Cryptographic KeyCritical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and FacilitiesCountries/Areas Deployed: WorldwideCompany Headquarters Location: GermanyA BIOS vendor test key is present in the UEFI Secure Boot key database. This could allow a local attacker with physical or administrative access to the device to boot an operating system or UEFI application signed with that test key, bypassing UEFI Secure Boot protections even when Secure Boot is enabled, potentially leading to a full loss of confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the device.SIMATIC IPC BX-21A < V31.01.13Product Status: known_affectedNote: After upgrading to the fixed BIOS version, users must load the BIOS default settings. If Secure Boot keys were already provisioned, they must be provisioned again afterwards.As a temporary mitigation, users can manually remove the test key from the database (e.g., "DO NOT TRUST - AMI Test PK" for RW-543A or "insyde-ElkhartLake" for IPC227G/277G/327G/377G and BX-21A). Note: Loading default settings will restore the test key, so upgrading remains recommended.Update to V31.01.13 or later versionSIMATIC IPC RW-543A < V1.1.4Product Status: known_affectedNote: After upgrading to the fixed BIOS version, users must load the BIOS default settings. If Secure Boot keys were already provisioned, they must be provisioned again afterwards.As a temporary mitigation, users can manually remove the test key from the database (e.g., "DO NOT TRUST - AMI Test PK" for RW-543A or "insyde-ElkhartLake" for IPC227G/277G/327G/377G and BX-21A). Note: Loading default settings will restore the test key, so upgrading remains recommended.Update to V1.1.4 or later versionSIMATIC IPC227G / IPC277G / IPC277G PRO / IPC327G / IPC377G < V28.01.15Product Status: known_affectedNote: After upgrading to the fixed BIOS version, users must load the BIOS default settings. If Secure Boot keys were already provisioned, they must be provisioned again afterwards.As a temporary mitigation, users can manually remove the test key from the database (e.g., "DO NOT TRUST - AMI Test PK" for RW-543A or "insyde-ElkhartLake" for IPC227G/277G/327G/377G and BX-21A). Note: Loading default settings will restore the test key, so upgrading remains recommended.Update to V28.01.15 or later versionSiemens ProductCERT reported this vulnerability to CISA.As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurityFor further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisoriesThe use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.Advisory Conversion DisclaimerThis ICSA is a verbatim republication of Siemens ProductCERT SSA-159454 from a direct conversion of the vendor's Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF) advisory. This is republished to CISA's website as a means of increasing visibility and is provided "as-is" for informational purposes only. CISA is not responsible for the editorial or technical accuracy of republished advisories and provides no warranties of any kind regarding any information contained within this advisory. Further, CISA does not endorse any commercial product or service. item.title: Siemens PSS(R)SINCAL
item.author: CISA
item.content:encoded: PSS(R)SINCAL uses WibuKey third-party product that contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to cause a system crash, resulting in a denial-of-service condition. This affects PSS SINCAL only when configured to use the legacy WibuKey dongle license type. Siemens is actively preparing updates and recommends applicable mitigations for products where patches are currently unavailable.The following versions of Siemens PSS(R)SINCAL are affected:PSS(R)SINCAL V21.5 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-84854)PSS(R)SINCAL V22.0 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-84854)PSS(R)SINCAL V22.5 vers:intdot/<22.5.5 (CVE-2026-84854)Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and FacilitiesCountries/Areas Deployed: WorldwideCompany Headquarters Location: GermanyIn the WibuKey driver, insufficient validation of user input when calculating the size of a kernel buffer could cause small amounts of data to be written outside the intended kernel buffer. This can lead to a system crash. Under unfavorable circumstances, adjacent kernel memory may be modified.Product Status: known_affectedInstall WIBU Systems WibuKey Runtime for Windows 6.72 or later version manually to fix the issue: Download the package from User Software - Wibu-Systems and follow the installation instructions from WIBU Systems.Currently no fix is availableProduct Status: known_affectedInstall WIBU Systems WibuKey Runtime for Windows 6.72 or later version manually to fix the issue: Download the package from User Software - Wibu-Systems and follow the installation instructions from WIBU Systems.Currently no fix is availablePSS(R)SINCAL V22.5 < V22.5 Update 5Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V22.5 Update 5 or later versionSiemens ProductCERT reported this vulnerability to CISA.Operators of critical power systems (e.g. TSOs or DSOs) worldwide are usually required by regulations to build resilience into the power grids by applying multi-level redundant secondary protection schemes. It is therefore recommended that the operators check whether appropriate resilient protection measures are in place. The risk of cyber incidents impacting the grid's reliability can thus be minimized by virtue of the grid design. Siemens strongly recommends applying the provided security updates using the corresponding tooling and documented procedures made available with the product. If supported by the product, an automated means to apply the security updates across multiple product instances may be used. Siemens strongly recommends prior validation of any security update before being applied, and supervision by trained staff of the update process in the target environment. As a general security measure Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access with appropriate mechanisms (e.g. firewalls, segmentation, VPN). It is advised to configure the environment according to our operational guidelines in order to run the devices in a protected IT environment.For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisoriesThe use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.Advisory Conversion DisclaimerThis ICSA is a verbatim republication of Siemens ProductCERT SSA-148322 from a direct conversion of the vendor's Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF) advisory. This is republished to CISA's website as a means of increasing visibility and is provided "as-is" for informational purposes only. CISA is not responsible for the editorial or technical accuracy of republished advisories and provides no warranties of any kind regarding any information contained within this advisory. Further, CISA does not endorse any commercial product or service. Please contact Siemens ProductCERT directly for any questions regarding this advisory.2026-10-13Initial CISA Republication of Siemens ProductCERT SSA-148322 advisoryLegal Notice and Terms of Use

item.title: Siemens SENTRON 3NA COM Fuse
item.author: CISA
item.content:encoded: SENTRON 3NA COM Fuse contains a Denial-of-Service vulnerability. Improper handling of a network management message could allow an attacker to trigger a denial-of-service (DoS) condition. Successful exploitation may require the affected network to be re-established to restore normal operation.The following versions of Siemens SENTRON 3NA COM Fuse are affected:SENTRON 3NA COM Fuse vers:intdot/<5.2 (CVE-2024-7322)Improper Verification of Source of a Communication ChannelCritical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and FacilitiesCountries/Areas Deployed: WorldwideCompany Headquarters Location: GermanyA ZigBee coordinator, router, or end device may change their node ID when an unsolicited encrypted rejoin response is received, this change in node ID causes Denial of Service (DoS). To recover from this DoS, the network must be re-establishedSENTRON 3NA COM Fuse < V5.2Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V5.2 or later versionSiemens ProductCERT reported this vulnerability to CISA.As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurityFor further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisoriesThe use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.Advisory Conversion DisclaimerThis ICSA is a verbatim republication of Siemens ProductCERT SSA-099819 from a direct conversion of the vendor's Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF) advisory. CISA is not responsible for the editorial or technical accuracy of republished advisories and provides no warranties of any kind regarding any information contained within this advisory. item.title: Siemens Software Center
item.author: CISA
item.content:encoded: The affected application loads dynamic-link libraries (DLLs) from an uncontrolled search path. This could allow an authenticated local attacker to place a specially crafted DLL in a directory that the application searches, leading to arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the affected application. Siemens has released a new version for Siemens Software Center and recommends to update to the latest version. Please refer to our blog post for additional information about current known active exploitation and how to detect it.The following versions of Siemens Software Center are affected:Siemens Software Center vers:intdot/<4.0.9.8 (CVE-2026-110936)Uncontrolled Search Path ElementCritical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and FacilitiesCountries/Areas Deployed: WorldwideCompany Headquarters Location: GermanyThe affected application loads dynamic-link libraries (DLLs) from an uncontrolled search path. item.title: Siemens Industrial Edge App Publisher
item.author: CISA
item.content:encoded: The Industrial Edge App Publisher contains a vulnerability chain involving improper certificate validation and the rendering of unescaped data from backend responses. These issues can be combined to allow an attacker on the network to impersonate the management server and execute arbitrary code (RCE) on the local machine through Node.js integration. Siemens has released an update for the Industrial Edge App Publisher and recommends to update to the latest version.The following versions of Siemens Industrial Edge App Publisher are affected:Industrial Edge App Publisher vers:intdot/<1.27.9 (CVE-2026-78556, CVE-2026-78557)Industrial Edge App PublisherImproper Certificate Validation, Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and FacilitiesCountries/Areas Deployed: WorldwideCompany Headquarters Location: GermanyThe affected software does not properly validate the server certificate when initiating a TLS connection. This allows an attacker to intercept and relay communication (Man-in-the-Middle attack) and to spoof a trusted entity by interfering in the communication path between the client and the intended server.Industrial Edge App Publisher < V1.27.9Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V1.27.9 or later versionThe application fails to properly sanitize or escape data received from the backend before rendering it in the user interface. Because the front end is integrated with Node.js, this vulnerability allows for the execution of arbitrary JavaScript, which can be leveraged to achieve remote code execution (RCE) on the victim's machineIndustrial Edge App Publisher < V1.27.9Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V1.27.9 or later versionIndustrial Edge App Publisher < V1.27.9Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V1.27.9 or later versionSiemens ProductCERT reported these vulnerabilities to CISA.As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurityFor further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisoriesThe use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.Advisory Conversion DisclaimerThis ICSA is a verbatim republication of Siemens ProductCERT SSA-968435 from a direct conversion of the vendor's Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF) advisory. item.title: Kiloview E3 NDI Encoder
item.author: CISA
item.content:encoded: Successful exploitation of this these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to fully compromise the device.The following versions of Kiloview E3 NDI Encoder are affected:E3 Firmware <1.30 (CVE-2026-109122, CVE-2026-111100, CVE-2026-96616, CVE-2026-105265, CVE-2026-110491, CVE-2026-107861, CVE-2026-110243, CVE-2026-92450, CVE-2026-110825)Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection'), Missing Authentication for Critical Function, Insufficient Session Expiration, Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal'), NULL Pointer Dereference, Use of Hard-coded CredentialsCritical Infrastructure Sectors: Communications, Information TechnologyCountries/Areas Deployed: WorldwideCompany Headquarters Location: ChinaThe network management service on affected Kiloview E3 NDI encoder firmware fails to sanitize one field used when configuring static routes via the web management API. An authenticated web user with permission to configure static routes can exploit this to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root, and the malicious configuration persists across reboots. Successful exploitation could result in full device compromise, including exposure of stored credentials and cryptographic material.Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/The ONVIF device service on the E3 responds to certain informational requests without requiring authentication. A remote, unauthenticated party can retrieve detailed device identifiers along with a list of configured user accounts and their privilege levels. This aids attackers in fingerprinting vulnerable devices and preparing targeted credential attacks.Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Authentication tokens issued by the E3's web management interface on login are given an expiration time far beyond any reasonable session lifetime, effectively making them non-expiring. A token obtained through interception or device compromise remains valid for authenticated access for an extended period.Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/A vulnerability exists in the the time zone parameter and does not properly validate user input, which may allow an authenticated user to cause /etc/localtime to point to a file outside the intended zoneinfo directoryKiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/The ONVIF service on the E3 can be rendered unresponsive by sending malformed or incomplete requests to certain operations. The affected service stops accepting new connections while the rest of the device continues operating normally, and will recover automatically after a period. This can be triggered repeatedly by any unauthenticated party with network access to the device.Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/The system control service on affected Kiloview E3 NDI encoder firmware fails to sanitize the hostname parameter accepted by its device naming endpoint, passing it unquoted into a shell command. An authenticated web user with access to this function can embed characters to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root, resulting in full device compromise.Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/The network management service on affected Kiloview E3 NDI encoder firmware fails to validate the network interface name accepted by its link maintenance address configuration endpoint before passing it to a shell command, unlike sibling handlers that perform the same validation. An authenticated web user with permission to configure network settings can exploit this to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root.Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/The authentication framework used by affected Kiloview E3 NDI encoder firmware signs session JSON Web Tokens using an HMAC-SHA256 secret hardcoded as a static string within the firmware image, identical across all deployed devices. An attacker with access to the publicly distributed firmware can recover this secret and forge arbitrary session tokens, including administrative tokens, without valid credentials, enabling unauthenticated access to privileged device functions.Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/The ONVIF device service on affected Kiloview E3 NDI encoder firmware accepts hostname, DNS, and NTP configuration write operations without requiring authentication, regardless of the device's configured authentication setting for this service. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can alter the device hostname, redirect DNS resolution, or modify the configured time source, enabling follow on attacks such as traffic interception or certificate validation bypass.Kiloview E3 Firmware: <1.30Product Status: known_affectedKiloView recommends users update to V1.30: https://www.kiloview.com/en/download/e3-firmware-downloadlatest-12/Kiloview E3 Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.CISA also recommends users take the following measures to protect themselves from social engineering attacks:No known public exploitation specifically targeting these vulnerabilities has been reported to CISA at this time.2026-10-22Legal Notice and Terms of Use

item.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
item.author: BrianKrebs
item.content:encoded: Expect to see quite a few websites serving error pages today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild.Image: Shutterstock.com, Sashkin.The flaws at issue are present in , the programming language that powers sites running on a large number of web publishing systems, including , , and . Earlier today, PHP released an emergency security update to fix two critical bugs that can allow an attacker to execute code of their choosing on a vulnerable server.reports that government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline today after the PHP vulnerabilities were disclosed. Cloudflare said it has already detected some exploitation of the flaw, and that at 3:02 am (UTC) it implemented web application firewall rules to protect websites from attack traffic seeking to exploit the bugs, which could cause a denial of service condition, remote code execution, and data exposure., which was involved in the vulnerability research and outreach, said “given the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory.”, a company that tracks the technology used by Internet hosts, said a recent scan identified approximately 2.58 million Internet facing hosts and 54.9 million web properties running PHP.Security experts at said every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities [full disclosure: Wiz is an advertiser on this blog].“These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history,” reads a blog post published today by a team of researchers at Wiz, which was one of several organizations credited with discovering the vulnerabilities. “The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve. Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit.”The Wiz researchers say it is likely the PHP vulnerabilities will be mass-exploited to install web-based backdoors or “web shells,” which give attackers a web-based panel that allows them to remotely control infected sites. Wiz said that prior to the PHP bugs being publicly disclosed, the company worked with the PHP team, Calif and OpenAI to measure the size of the problem and coordinate patch verification and disclosure.The PHP zero-day vulnerabilities are being tracked by their CVE numbers, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, and they affect all web servers running PHP 5.4 or later. The bugs are fixed in PHP , , , and .According to Wiz, PHP is so deeply embedded in many web applications that we are likely to see organizations struggling to patch these vulnerabilities for some time to come, comparing this PHP vulnerability pair with the Log4Shell weakness that emerged in 2021 — a widespread, severe-as-it-gets security flaw in Log4j, a popular Java logging framework.“A vulnerability in core PHP reaches far beyond a single application,” the Wiz researchers wrote. “PHP runs across clouds, hosting providers, content-delivery networks and millions of independently managed servers. Reducing exposure before the technical details became public required coordinated work across that entire ecosystem.”The SANS Internet Storm Center is keeping an eye on major software platforms that are shipping updates to deal with these PHP flaws. For example, Ubuntu just released updated PHP packages. For a technical deep-dive on these vulnerabilities that tells the timeline of the discovery of these bugs in a comic book style, check out this post from , another technology company credited with finding the PHP flaws.A snapshot of php2shell.censys.com, the website Censys set up to track the PHP vulnerabilities.This is a fast-moving story. Updates will be noted here with timestamps. Add figures from Censys and a link to Calif’s writeup.

item.title: Hitachi Energy MicroSCADA X SYS600 Product
item.author: CISA
item.content:encoded: Hitachi Energy is aware of multiple vulnerabilities that affect MicroSCADA X SYS600 product versions listed in this document. These vulnerabilities can be exploited to carry out various attacks on the product. Please refer to the Recommended Immediate Actions for information about the mitigation/remediation.The following versions of Hitachi Energy MicroSCADA X SYS600 Product are affected:MicroSCADA X SYS600 vers:MicroSCADA_X_SYS600/<=10.7, 10.8 (CVE-2026-9852, CVE-2026-9853, CVE-2026-9854, CVE-2026-9853)Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File, Incorrect Implementation of Authentication AlgorithmCritical Infrastructure Sectors: EnergyCountries/Areas Deployed: WorldwideCompany Headquarters Location: SwitzerlandA CSV injection vulnerability exists in SYS600. Injected malicious formulas can add or modify data to the spreadsheet, insert links, exfiltrate data, and in some cases, depending on how the user has their environment configured, execute malicious code on the user’s machine. To exploit this issue attackers would need a way to create arbitrary log messages. This could be achieved through normal functionality via SCIL scripts, a log injection vulnerability, or via the SYS600 broker. This vulnerability affects all Windows users regardless of their privilege level who can run the Notify service and export the log.MicroSCADA X SYS600 versions 10.7 and priorProduct Status: known_affectedUpdate to version 10.8Follow general mitigation factors/workaroundsA vulnerability exists in SYS600 which allows any user authenticated to the operating system of the server hosting the application to read and modify application objects without being authenticated to the SYS600 system itself. Only the SYS600 system users should be permitted to view and modify application objects.MicroSCADA X SYS600 versions 10.7 and priorProduct Status: known_affectedUpdate to version 10.8 and Follow mitigation strategy. For contact information, see https://www.hitachienergy.com/contact-us/ for Hitachi Energy contact-centers.General Mitigation FactorsRecommended security practices and firewall configurations can help protect a process control network from attacks that originate from outside the network. Such practices include that process control systems are physically protected from direct access by unauthorized personnel, have no direct connections to the Internet, and are separated from other networks by means of a firewall system that has a minimal number of ports exposed, and others that have to be evaluated case by case. Process control systems should not be used for Internet surfing, instant messaging, or receiving e-mails. Portable computers and removable storage media should be carefully scanned for viruses before they are connected to a control system. Proper password policies and processes should be followed. Please refer to the Recommended Immediate Actions for information about the mitigation/remediation.The following versions of Hitachi Energy RTU500 Product are affected:RTU500 series CMU Firmware vers:RTU500_series_CMU_Firmware/>=13.5.1|<=13.5.4, vers:RTU500_series_CMU_Firmware/>=13.6.1|<=13.6.3, vers:RTU500_series_CMU_Firmware/>=13.7.1|<=13.7.8, vers:RTU500_series_CMU_Firmware/>=13.8.1|<=13.8.2, vers:RTU500_series_CMU_Firmware/>=12.7.1|<=12.7.7 (CVE-2026-17539, CVE-2026-28388, CVE-2026-6732, CVE-2026-6653, CVE-2026-6276, CVE-2026-9079, CVE-2026-11856, CVE-2026-8927, CVE-2026-8932, CVE-2026-17539, CVE-2026-28388, CVE-2026-6732, CVE-2026-6653, CVE-2026-6276, CVE-2026-9079, CVE-2026-11856, CVE-2026-8927, CVE-2026-8932, CVE-2026-17539, CVE-2026-28388, CVE-2026-6732, CVE-2026-6653, CVE-2026-6276, CVE-2026-9079, CVE-2026-11856, CVE-2026-8927, CVE-2026-8932, CVE-2026-17539, CVE-2026-28388, CVE-2026-6732, CVE-2026-6653, CVE-2026-6276, CVE-2026-9079, CVE-2026-11856, CVE-2026-8927, CVE-2026-8932, CVE-2026-17539, CVE-2026-28388, CVE-2026-6653)RTU500 series CMU FirmwareNULL Pointer Dereference, Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion'), Use After Free, Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information, Insufficiently Protected Credentials, Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay, Authentication Bypass by Primary WeaknessCritical Infrastructure Sectors: EnergyCountries/Areas Deployed: WorldwideCompany Headquarters Location: SwitzerlandRTU500 has a vulnerability, where high-load scenarios, such as sending GI requests at short intervals, may cause a NULL pointer dereference in the last entry of the enhanced message queue. This can cause a BCI_IEC104 fatal write error, resulting in connection interruption and restart, and ultimately a denial of service for bidirectional IEC 60870-5-104 communication.RTU500 series CMU Firmware version 13.5.1 – 13.5.4Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to CMU Firmware version 13.9.1Follow general mitigation factors/workaroundsRTU500 series CMU Firmware version 13.6.1 – 13.6.3Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to CMU Firmware version 13.9.1Follow general mitigation factors/workaroundsRTU500 series CMU Firmware version 13.7.1 – 13.7.8Product Status: known_affectedFollow general mitigation factors/workaroundsUpdate to CMU Firmware version 13.9.1 or 13.7.9 (when available)RTU500 series CMU Firmware version 13.8.1 – 13.8.2Product Status: known_affectedFollow general mitigation factors/workaroundsUpdate to CMU Firmware version 13.9.1 or 13.8.3*RTU500 series CMU Firmware version 12.7.1 – 12.7.7Product Status: known_affectedFollow general mitigation factors/workaroundsUpdate to CMU Firmware version 12.7.8 ORUpgrade to CMU Firmware version 13.9.1A vulnerability exists in OpenSSL library component of RTU500 that is used for secure HTTPS access, authenticating and establishing encrypted communications with other devices. When processing a malformed delta CRL with a Delta CRL Indicator but no required CRL Number extension, OpenSSL may dereference a NULL pointer, causing a Denial of Service during X.509 certificate verification. Exploitation requires delta CRL processing to be enabled, a relevant freshest CRL condition to be present, and an attacker-supplied malformed CRL. The issue is limited to Denial of Service and cannot lead to code execution or memory disclosure.RTU500 series CMU Firmware version 13.5.1 – 13.5.4Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to CMU Firmware All rights to registrations and trademarks reside with their respective owners.For additional information and support please contact your product provider or Hitachi Energy service organization. For contact information, see https://www.hitachienergy.com/contact-us/ for Hitachi Energy contact-centers.General Mitigation FactorsRecommended security practices and firewall configurations can help protect a process control network from attacks that originate from outside the network. Such practices include that process control systems are physically protected from direct access by unauthorized personnel, have no direct connections to the Internet, and are separated from other networks by means of a firewall system that has a minimal number of ports exposed, and others that have to be evaluated case by case. Process control systems should not be used for Internet surfing, instant messaging, or receiving e-mails. Portable computers and removable storage media should be carefully scanned for viruses before they are connected to a control system. Proper password policies and processes should be followed. Additional information on Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity Best Practices can be found in the Hitachi Energy “Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity Best Practices” Cybersecurity Notification. [1]SSVCv2/E:N/A:N/2026-09-28T14:29:30Z/CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the exploitation risk of this vulnerability.Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, and ensure they are not accessible from the internet.Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolate them from business networks.When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most recent version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as its connected devices.CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets. Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.Advisory Conversion DisclaimerThis ICSA is a verbatim republication of Hitachi Energy PSIRT 8DBD000259 from a direct conversion of the vendor's Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF) advisory. item.title: Moxa AIG-302 ThingsPro Edge
item.author: CISA
item.content:encoded: Moxa Moxa AIG-302 ThingsPro Edge firmware: <=1.4.0Product Status: known_affectedMoxa has provided a fix for the vulnerability in v1.4.1. Users are encouraged to obtain and apply the update through one of the following methods:If the AIG-302 has Internet access, login to the AIG-302 Web Console, go to Maintenance > Software Upgrades, and click Check for upgrades to check for and obtain the update.Users can download the v1.4.1 patch manually from either the official AIG-302 product website or the Moxa Software Release Service. Then, log in to the AIG-302 Web Console, navigate to Maintenance > Software Upgrades, and select Package Upload to upload the patch.Users can download the v1.4.1 patch manually from either the official AIG-302 product website or the Moxa Software Release Service. item.title: Possible new Cellebrite iPhone Radio Zero-Day
item.author: Bruce Schneier
item.content:encoded: Justin.sh is reporting on a confidential Cellebrite document that has been leaked to him:Cellebrite calls it Advanced Unlocks (AU from here on), not to be confused with the “advanced unlocking services” they’ve marketed for years. A press release from earlier this year confirms AU is a new product for 2026.According to Cellebrite, AU:is a “next-generation AFU vector that is more resilient to Apple’s OS changes” works with Stolen Device Protection enabled, which tightens USB restrictions is enabled by a dedicated appliance with a stated range (!) of about 8 meters.AU = Advanced Unlocks, Cellebrite’s term. AFU = after first unlock.
